outputs.L1: A new method, FM-FTS, combining frequency-modulation heterodyne laser spectroscopy with Fourier-transform spectroscopy, is presented. It enables the simultaneous, sensitive measurement of absorption and dispersion profiles while providing broadband spectral coverage. The method is experimentally demonstrated using the overtone spectrum of C₂H₂ in the 1.5 μm region.
outputs.L2: We introduce FM-FTS, a technique that integrates frequency-modulation heterodyne laser spectroscopy with Fourier-transform spectroscopy. This approach enables highly sensitive, simultaneous detection of absorption and dispersion line shapes across a broad spectral range. Its performance is demonstrated experimentally using the overtone spectrum of C₂H₂ near 1.5 μm.
outputs.L3: Frequency Modulation Fourier Transform Spectroscopy (FM-FTS) combines the high sensitivity of frequency-modulation heterodyne laser spectroscopy with the broad spectral coverage of Fourier transform spectroscopy. By integrating these two approaches, FM-FTS enables the simultaneous measurement of both absorption and dispersion profiles, providing complementary information about molecular transitions. The method therefore supports sensitive detection across a wide spectral range while retaining the multiplex advantages of Fourier transform techniques. Its performance was experimentally demonstrated through measurements of the overtone spectrum of acetylene (C₂H₂) in the 1.5 μm wavelength region.
outputs.L4:
Frequency-modulation Fourier-transform spectroscopy (FM-FTS) combines the high sensitivity of frequency-modulation heterodyne laser spectroscopy with the broad spectral coverage and multiplex capability of Fourier-transform spectroscopy. In this approach, a broadband optical source is frequency-modulated before interacting with the sample. The transmitted radiation is then analyzed with a Fourier-transform spectrometer, while heterodyne detection isolates the modulation-induced signals. Because the detected response contains both absorptive and dispersive components, the technique can simultaneously recover molecular absorption line shapes and the associated phase or refractive-index variations across a wide spectral interval.

The use of modulation and phase-sensitive detection strongly suppresses background fluctuations and low-frequency technical noise, improving sensitivity relative to conventional broadband absorption measurements. At the same time, Fourier-transform analysis avoids the need to scan individual transitions one by one. FM-FTS can therefore record many spectral features in parallel while retaining access to detailed line-shape information. Simultaneous measurements of absorption and dispersion also provide complementary constraints for determining transition frequencies, linewidths, intensities, and other molecular parameters.

The method has been demonstrated using the overtone spectrum of acetylene, C₂H₂, near 1.5 μm. The resulting spectra show that weak molecular features can be detected over a broad wavelength range and that both the absorptive and dispersive profiles can be extracted from the same measurement. This demonstration confirms that FM-FTS offers a sensitive and versatile platform for broadband molecular detection.

By uniting heterodyne sensitivity with Fourier-transform spectral coverage, FM-FTS is well suited to comprehensive molecular spectroscopy. Potential applications include trace-gas sensing, precision line-shape studies, atmospheric monitoring, combustion diagnostics, and laboratory investigations of complex molecular bands.
outputs.L5:
### FTS, Frequency, and Modulation

Fourier Transform Spectroscopy (FTS) is a measurement technique used to analyze how matter interacts with electromagnetic radiation across a broad range of frequencies. Instead of measuring each frequency separately, an FTS instrument records an interference pattern known as an interferogram. A Fourier transform then converts this signal into a spectrum, revealing the frequency components absorbed or emitted by the sample.

Frequency modulation can enhance FTS measurements. In this method, the frequency of the radiation source is varied periodically around a central value. When the modulated signal interacts with a sample, small spectral changes can be detected more effectively through phase-sensitive detection. This approach improves sensitivity, reduces background noise, and helps distinguish weak spectral features.

The combination of FTS and frequency modulation is valuable in fields such as chemical analysis, atmospheric monitoring, astronomy, and molecular spectroscopy. It provides broad spectral coverage together with high resolution and accurate frequency information, making it particularly useful for identifying substances and studying their physical properties.

counterfactuals.output: We present a spectroscopic technique that combines frequency-modulation heterodyne detection with Fourier-transform spectroscopy. A phase-modulated laser source passes through the sample and is analyzed by a Fourier-transform interferometer, while demodulation at the modulation frequency isolates absorption- and dispersion-sensitive heterodyne signals. This approach couples the broad spectral coverage and multiplex capability of Fourier-transform spectroscopy with the high sensitivity, background suppression, and near-shot-noise performance of frequency-modulation methods. The technique enables rapid, high-resolution measurements of weak spectral features with improved rejection of laser-intensity noise and baseline fluctuations.
